questions.q: When Theo splits checkout-api's pods by availability zone, what does he find?
options: The twelve pods are split evenly, four per zone
Eight of the twelve pods are running in a single zone, eastus2-2, while the other two zones have only two pods each
All twelve pods are in one zone and none in the others
The pods are spread across six different zones
questions.explain: The per-zone pod listing shows eastus2-2 running eight of the twelve checkout-api pods, with eastus2-1 and eastus2-3 holding only two each.

questions.q: What are the real per-zone CPU utilization numbers Theo finds, and how do they relate to the 72% cluster-wide average?
options: Every zone is at exactly 72% — the average was accurate all along
eastus2-2's 8 pods run at ~96% while eastus2-1 and eastus2-3's pods run at ~24% each; blended together these produce the 72% average
All zones are at 0% because the pods are not actually running
The per-zone numbers cannot be computed from pod-level CPU data
questions.explain: (96×8 + 24×2 + 24×2) / 12 ≈ 72% — the average is mathematically correct, but it blends a saturated zone with two nearly-idle ones into a number that looks healthy.

questions.q: Is kube-scheduler malfunctioning by packing eight pods into one zone?
options: Yes, this is a scheduler bug that needs a Kubernetes upgrade
No — the scheduler is bin-packing efficiently exactly as designed; nothing in the Deployment spec told it to spread pods across zones
Yes, because schedulers always spread pods evenly by default
It's impossible to know without contacting Microsoft support
questions.explain: kube-scheduler packs pods onto nodes with available capacity unless a topology spread constraint or anti-affinity rule tells it to do otherwise — and checkout-api's Deployment spec has neither.

questions.q: What exact root cause does Theo identify in the checkout-api Deployment spec built back in Lesson 4?
options: Too many replicas were requested
The missing topologySpreadConstraints / pod anti-affinity rule — nothing ever told the scheduler to distribute pods evenly across zones
The wrong container image was deployed
The Deployment has no CPU requests set at all
questions.explain: The AKS cluster and checkout-api Deployment were never given a topology spread constraint or anti-affinity rule, so the scheduler was free to pack pods wherever was efficient — which, under this sale's traffic, meant stacking most of them into one zone.

questions.q: Why does this lesson mark the turning point of the incident?
options: Because the sale has ended
Because the problem has gone from a confusing metric disagreement to a specific, fixable bug — a missing scheduling constraint
Because the FinOps dashboard has been deleted
Because Theo has decided to ignore the reliability dashboard going forward
questions.explain: Once the per-zone data traces the imbalance to a missing topology spread constraint, the team has a concrete, fixable root cause instead of an open question.
